result.title: Certified Defense against Adversarial Patches on Traffic Signs via Mask-Aware Training
result.summary: Adversarial patches are a practical threat to traffic-sign recognition: a small sticker on a sign can change a classifier's decision. PatchCleanser is a certified defense that applies two rounds of masking and, for every image it certifies, provably returns the correct label for any patch that fits inside one mask. We show that on traffic signs the defense certifies almost nothing when paired with a normally trained classifier (1.7% to 4.8% certified accuracy on GTSRB), because a single mask can hide the small central symbol that distinguishes sign classes. We propose mask-aware training, which trains the classifier on images occluded by random pairs drawn from the defense's own mask set, with a sampling bias toward masks over the sign's centre. The defense, mask set and certification procedure are unchanged, so the guarantee is preserved. For an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, mask-aware training raises certified accuracy from 4.8% to 60.0%. Under real per-image adversarial patches, the defended ResNet-50 reaches 85.7% accuracy, versus 74.6% for the original PatchCleanser with a normally trained ResNet-50.

AI.brief_summary: 研究交通标志上对抗补丁的认证防御：发现 PatchCleanser 搭配常规训练分类器时认证准确率极低（GTSRB 仅 1.7%–4.8%），因为单个掩码可遮住区分类别的中心符号；作者提出 mask-aware training，在防御自身掩码集合的随机成对遮挡图上训练（偏向遮挡标志中心），掩码集合与认证流程不变，ResNet-50 认证准确率从 4.8% 升至 60.0%。
